lesson_title: Report Card Day: Final Accounts and the Year-End Run
hook_text: You can't photocopy a diary and call it a report card.
clip_script: All year, the shop wrote its own diary — every sale, every payment, day by day. Now comes report card day: one page answering the owner's two oldest questions — did we make money, and how much? But here's the catch: some diary lines have drifted from the truth. The stationery page says R1 000 spent — but R200 of it still sits unused in the cupboard. The stock page claims R2 400 — count the shelf: R2 250. The shelf wins. Always. So year-end has two jobs, in strict order: TIDY the diary until it matches the real shop — those are the adjustments. THEN squeeze it through two sieves: the first catches the buying-and-selling story — gross profit, R20 000. The second drains away every running cost — net profit, R11 500. And that number pours into the owner's jar, where it always belonged.
visual_style: A handwritten diary morphing into a single report card; a cupboard and shelf glowing where reality disagrees; then two animated sieves pouring numbers down into a jar labelled Capital.
pacing: Calm setup, two sharp reality-check beats, accelerating pour through the sieves to the final number.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run a whole year to its true profit.
